headline: HALTER reports autonomous resets for long-horizon robot evaluations
summary: An arXiv paper introduces HALTER, a system for scoring and resetting real-robot long-horizon manipulation trials. On one Franka Panda arm, the authors report successful resets in 76% of 100 episodes across four tasks, compared with 52% for AutoEval and 65% for a motion-planning baseline; reset-verification accuracy is 91%, and operator time is 24 versus 88 minutes for manual resets. On three held-out tasks, HALTER reportedly resets 74.7% of episodes versus 1.3% for per-task reset. Results are author-reported, limited to one robot and seven tabletop tasks; one main task favors the motion-planning baseline.
